pages.name: Still there?
pages.task: A jack's small piston has an area of 10 cm². Its big piston has an area of 200 cm². You push the small one down with 100 N. What load can the big one hold up?
pages.why: 100 N on 10 cm² makes 10 N on every square centimetre. The oil carries that pressure to all 200 cm² of the big piston. So the big piston holds up 2000 N.

pages.name: Built from marks
pages.text: A fluid power symbol is built from a few marks. Each mark means one thing. A large circle is usually a machine that turns. A solid triangle is oil, pointing the way it flows. Oil flowing out of the circle makes it a pump. Here a circle and a solid triangle pointing out of it are named Hydraulic pump, fixed.

pages.name: Flip it
pages.task: The triangle now points into the circle. What is the part?
pages.why: Oil flowing in turns the shaft, so the part is a motor. In a pump the triangle's point touches the circle. In a motor its flat side does.

pages.name: Empty means air
pages.text: An empty triangle means air instead of oil. Pointing out, it makes a [[compressor]]. Pointing in, it makes an air motor. Here the triangle is empty and points out, so the part is named Air compressor, fixed.

pages.name: Count the air
pages.task: How many of these five parts run on air?
pages.why: The air motor and the compressor have empty triangles. The other three have solid ones, so they run on oil.

pages.name: The adjusting arrow
pages.text: A slanted arrow across a part means it can be adjusted. Across a pump, it means the volume each turn delivers can be changed. Here the arrow is drawn across the circle, and the part is named Hydraulic pump, variable.

pages.name: Build one
pages.task: Which marks make an air motor you can adjust?
pages.answer: Circle, empty triangle in, slanted arrow
pages.why: Air is the empty triangle. A motor's triangle points in. The arrow makes it adjustable.

pages.text: The symbol says what a part does, not how it is built. A gear pump and a piston pump are nothing alike inside. If each delivers a fixed volume each turn, both take this one symbol. pages.task: What does this symbol tell you about the real pump?
pages.answer: It pumps oil, a fixed volume each turn
pages.why: The solid triangle pointing out makes it a hydraulic pump. No arrow means fixed. How it is built and where its ports sit come from the part or its data sheet.

pages.name: The rest of the kit
pages.text: Other parts use the same marks. A diamond treats the fluid. A dashed line across it makes a filter. Arrowheads pointing out of it make a cooler. A box with a piston and rod is a cylinder. An open-topped box is the tank. An upright capsule stores oil under pressure. A small circle with a pointer inside is a gauge. Here the six finished symbols are each matched to their card: tank, cylinder, filter, cooler, accumulator and pressure gauge.

pages.name: Turned on its side
pages.task: These two symbols sit on one sheet. What are they?
pages.why: Both are diamonds with a dashed line across, so both are filters. Most symbols mean the same however they are turned on the sheet. A tank and the lines into it are the exception, and stay as drawn.

pages.name: Read the power unit
pages.task: What is the circle the electric motor drives?
pages.why: Solid means oil, and out means it pumps. The arrow makes it adjustable. So the electric motor drives a variable hydraulic pump. The small circle on the line out is a gauge. Its pointer stays inside it, while the adjusting arrow crosses the whole pump.

pages.task: How many of the circles on this sheet are pumps?
pages.why: The upright pump and the pump on its side have triangles pointing out. The hydraulic motor's points in. The electric motor and the gauge have none. So 2 are pumps.
